name: FortiGate — Internal Host Beaconing to Malicious/C2 Domain (DNS)
description:
Attacker objective
An infected internal host beacons to attacker command-and-control or crypto-mining infrastructure via DNS.

Attack logic
DNS filtering blocks or redirects lookups to known-malicious domains. Internal DNS resolvers forward all client queries and are excluded; a non-resolver endpoint generating repeated blocked malicious-domain lookups is an infected host beaconing.

Why this detection works
Threat-feed-backed DNS verdicts, plus a resolver/forwarder allowlist, attribute the malicious lookups to the true endpoint (source IP/MAC) rather than the resolver that forwards them.

False positives
A shared NAT/proxy not in the resolver allowlist; an occasional user typo.

Tuning
Maintain the resolver/forwarder allowlist; adjust the count for chatty hosts.

Required telemetry
FortiGate DNS-filter UTM (subtype:dns, blocked/redirect action, dns.question.name, source.ip, source.mac).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip / source.mac = the infected endpoint; dns.question.name = the C2/malware domain.
2. Isolate and scan the host; hunt for the malware family (e.g. crypto-miner, botnet).
3. Correlate with lateral-movement / exploit alerts on the same host.
false_positives: A shared NAT/proxy not in the resolver allowlist; an occasional user typo.
query: fortinet.firewall.subtype:"dns" and fortinet.firewall.action:"redirect" and not source.ip:("192.168.112.222" or "192.168.112.223" or "192.168.25.1" or "172.17.25.1" or "192.168.112.221")
